title.purpose: Section titles and the chat box question.

body.purpose: Running text, input values, helper copy.

body-semibold.purpose: Stop and row titles: the names you scan down the route.

body-strong.purpose: Button text, plan titles in lists, terminus and stage names.

numeral.purpose: Stop times in the time column; all times and counts use tabular figures at 800.

label.purpose: Form labels, guide words in the band, quiet buttons, prompt chips, error text.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default curve: press, marker transform, check stroke, route-draw.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: The travelling dot while a plan drafts.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Every tappable element answers the thumb; background and border colours also ease over 160ms.

motion.name: marker-fill
motion.purpose: A stop's marker changes state the moment Done or Skip is tapped (optimistic).

motion.name: check-stroke
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset 24 -> 0 over 260ms var(--ease-out), 60ms delay, entered via @starting-style
motion.purpose: The check draws itself into a done marker.

motion.name: route-draw
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: Today's route draws itself downward once on open.

motion.name: travel
motion.purpose: The drafting indicator: a yellow stop travelling a short dashed line; the only loop.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Reduced motion removes the route-draw, the travelling dot and the press scale.

narrative.overview:
Stride draws the day as a route. Every task step, habit session and study block is a stop on one 4px green line that runs down the left of the screen: solid behind you, dashed ahead, with a yellow "you are here" stop at the current time. The screen always answers two questions at a glance: where am I, and what is next. Plans use the same grammar. A task is a line ending at its deadline terminus, a skill is a line of milestone stations grouped by stage, and a habit is a loop of daily stops. The system refuses the category default of a checkbox list in white cards.

The material is Lagos route-line signage: a cool green-tinted ground, deep green ink, one Stride green that carries the header band, the line, primary buttons and finished stops, and danfo yellow kept for the present moment. Overpass, a typeface with road-sign lineage, sets everything, with heavy tabular numerals for times. Colour is flat. Depth comes from the green band over the tinted ground and from white panels resting on it, never from shadows.

Density is calm and thumb-first. Visits last seconds, so hierarchy comes from scale and weight rather than labels: one large day name, one large next-stop title, everything else quiet. State is a mark on the stop, not a badge beside it. Missed stops get a red ring and a plain "Missed" note, and nothing scolds. Motion is spare: one authored route-draw when Today opens, and immediate answers to every touch.
keyCharacteristics: One green route per screen; stops carry state as marks (filled, crossed, red ring, green ring).
Yellow means now: the current time, today, the stop in progress.
Flat colour on a green-tinted ground; white panels; no shadows.
Overpass at three weights; tabular times; tracking only ever tightens.
Single centred column, bottom tab bar on phones, top bar on desktop.
Spare motion that always gives way to reduced-motion preferences.

rules.name: The Here-and-Now Rule
rules.body: Danfo Yellow marks the present moment and nothing else: the current time, today, the stop in progress. Its only other uses are functional, as the focus ring on green and as the selection highlight.

rules.name: The White-on-Green Rule
rules.body: Text on Route Green is Paper White or Mint Signage only, and the green stays dark enough for white text to clear 4.5:1. Never lighten the brand green toward the sketch's #0E8A4F.

rules.name: The Three Weights Rule
rules.body: Only 400, 600 and 800 are loaded. 400 is for reading, 600 for names, 800 for anything you act on or scan for: times, titles, buttons.

rules.name: The Plain Label Rule
rules.body: No eyebrows, kickers, uppercase labels or positive letter-spacing. Tracking only tightens, on display (-0.02em), headline and title (-0.01em) and the wordmark.

rules.name: The Centred Dot Rule
rules.body: Meta parts are joined by U+2219 "∙" with a space either side. Overpass sets the usual middle dot (U+00B7) off-centre, so it is not used.

rules.name: The Three Column Rule
rules.body: Anything drawn as a route uses the 52px time column, 40px rail column and flexible content column, so lines and markers align from screen to screen.

rules.name: The Flat Colour Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows, glows, blurs or smooth gradients. The only gradient in the system is the hard-stop pattern that draws the dashed route ahead, which reads as flat dashes.

rules.name: The Line Is A Background Rule
rules.body: The route line is a 4px background strip in the rail column: filled for the past, a hard-stop dash pattern for what is ahead. It is never a border or side stripe on a card or row.

rules.name: The Set-Apart Rule
rules.body: Final or destructive actions (Discard, Archive) are quiet buttons placed away from the primary action: Discard sits centred beneath the draft's Accept and Redraft, and Archive is pushed to the far end of its row.

rules.name: The One Moment Rule
rules.body: The route-draw on Today is the only authored entrance. Every other motion answers a touch (press scale, marker fill, check stroke) or a wait (the travelling dot), and reduced-motion preferences switch off the route-draw, the travelling dot and the press scale.

dos: Do draw every sequence of work as stops on one 4px Route Green line: solid behind the current time, dashed ahead (8px dashes every 14px).
Do show state as a mark on the stop: filled green with a check for done, grey ring and cross for skipped, red ring for missed, green ring for planned.
Do size stops by length with the fixed ramp (16px, 20px, 24px, 28px at 15, 30, 60 and more minutes) and draw glyphs only at 20px and up.
Do set every time and count in Overpass 800 with tabular figures.
Do join meta parts with U+2219 "∙" and a space either side: "Task ∙ 60 min ∙ step 3 of 4".
Do keep one next-stop card per screen and let it be the only bordered card.
Do give every tappable element the press response: scale 0.97 over 160ms, removed under reduced motion.
Do keep focus visible: a 3px Route Green outline at 2px offset, Danfo Yellow on green surfaces.
donts: Don't use yellow for anything but the present moment, the focus ring on green and the selection highlight.
Don't lighten the brand green toward #0E8A4F; white text on it falls to 4.4:1.
Don't add eyebrow or kicker labels above headings, and don't set uppercase or letter-spaced labels.
Don't use the U+00B7 middle dot as a separator; it sits off-centre in Overpass.
Don't draw the route line as a border or coloured side stripe on a card or row.
Don't add drop shadows, glows, blurs or smooth gradients.
Don't put state in badges or pills; the marker is the state.
Don't place Discard or Archive next to the primary action.
Don't load weights other than 400, 600 and 800, or a second typeface.
